claim: For a binary ecological incidence matrix with \(m\ge2\) rows, \(n\ge2\) columns, and no zero row or column, let \(\mathrm{NODF}\) be the classical normalized nestedness based on overlap and decreasing fill, averaged over all unordered row pairs and all unordered column pairs, with equal-degree pairs contributing zero. Put \(a=\min\{m,n\}\), \(b=\max\{m,n\}=qa+r\), where \(q\ge1\) and \(0\le r<a\), and \(K=\binom{m}{2}+\binom{n}{2}\). Without constraining the number of edges, the exact maximum is \(\max\mathrm{NODF}=1-[(a-r)\binom{q}{2}+r\binom{q+1}{2}]/K\). Equality holds exactly for Ferrers incidence matrices, up to independent row and column permutation and interchange of the two sides, in which the \(b\) vertices of the larger guild have degrees \(1,\ldots,a\), each degree appearing \(q\) or \(q+1\) times and exactly \(r\) degrees appearing \(q+1\) times. There are precisely \(\binom{a}{r}\) inequivalent maximizers for each fixed shape. When the guild sizes are unequal the maximum is strictly below one, while for fixed \(a\ge2\) and \(b\to\infty\) it tends to \(1-1/a\). This is a dimension-only ceiling: it is valid at every link count but need not be attainable when the number of edges is fixed.
integrity: The proof reduces the optimum to a sharp minimum of equal-degree pairs in the larger guild, constructs balanced Ferrers matrices attaining every pairwise upper bound, and characterizes equality. Exact integer-arithmetic enumeration of 176554 eligible small matrices independently confirms the formula and maximizer-type count.
scientific_limitations: Only classical binary, degree-tie-zero, all-pair normalized NODF on matrices with no isolated species and both guild sizes at least two is considered. The total number of links is unconstrained: for a fixed link count the achievable maximum may be strictly lower. No weighted, fixed-fill, or statistically adjusted nestedness conclusions are asserted.
title: Exact size-only NODF ceiling and Ferrers maximizers for rectangular ecological networks
